clue.text: A small amount of water causes lower rents

definitions.note: the plural answer names a few small drops, a small amount taken together

parts.note: to lower something is to drop it
lets are rentals, things rented out

explanation.surface: A landlord cutting rents has made only a tiny splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' and 'rents' read as an adjective and noun, but each is a verb-or-noun piece: DROP for lower, LETS for rents.
explanation.definitionFit: Droplets are tiny drops, so a few of them make only a little liquid.

clue.text: A lot of words properly pronounced only by judges

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit made of several words
the penalty a judge pronounces on a convicted person

explanation.surface: Lengthy speeches should properly be delivered only by those on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's unit of several words, and the court's penalty that a judge formally passes, share one name.

clue.text: Cut off a confession of excessive unpunctuality

definitions.meaning: to cut off is to set apart from others
split into three words, the letters say '...', the admission of someone very tardy

explanation.surface: A habitual latecomer is shunned after owning up yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something from all others is to cut it off; split as 'I so late' it is a latecomer's admission.

clue.text: Take the top form

definitions.meaning: in some British public schools a ... is a class or form, often a senior one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take the top sheet of a printed form.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'form' in a British school is a class or year group; the Remove is the name of such a class in some public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away is to shift something elsewhere; at certain British schools one class is named after the same word.

clue.text: They make light of upsets

definitions.meaning: thin strips of wood or paper used to light fires or pipes
a spill is an accidental upset or tumble

explanation.surface: Some people shrug off accidents and treat them lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden tapers used for kindling a flame, and accidental overturnings or falls, share one plural word.

clue.text: Given push it should clean up a pile

definitions.text: Given push it should clean up a pile

parts.words: Given push it should clean up a pile
parts.note: the pile is the raised nap of a rug, and the device cleans it when pushed across by hand

explanation.surface: A heap of mess will be tidied away if someone gives it a shove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pile' suggests a heap of rubbish; here it is the soft surface of a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-pushed machine with rotating brushes that lifts dirt from the nap of a rug.

clue.text: Homer using warship jargon, we hear

parts.note: an aircraft carrier is a warship

indicators.note: signals that the jargon word is matched by a different word that sounds the same

parts.note: pidgin is a simplified mixed language, loosely a jargon

explanation.surface: The poet Homer seemingly speaks in naval slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the Greek poet; it is a bird that flies home. 'we hear' turns PIDGIN into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing bird trained to return to its loft, used for carrying messages.

clue.text: Act as expected from king disloyal to class

parts.note: R stands for king, from Latin rex
someone disloyal is untrue
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A monarch proves treacherous to his own social class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' reads as social rank; it is a school form.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave in one's usual, predictable way is to act just as anticipated.

clue.text: Hollow demand by aggressive Scargillite

definitions.meaning: a hollow or cavity of the body, under the shoulder
a militant miner might order the colliery to take up arms

explanation.surface: A strident miner's union cry rings empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Scargill led Britain's miners' union in the bitter 1984-85 strike; a Scargillite is his follower, and a pit is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavity beneath the shoulder is a body hollow; split, the word is a call for a mine to take up weapons.

clue.text: Hitch which proves to be a diversion for train travellers

definitions.meaning: a hitch is a looped knot made in a line
a railway branch that leaves the main track and rejoins it further on

explanation.surface: A hold-up turns out to be a detour for rail passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope knotted into a ring is a hitch; a railway branch looping away from and back onto the main track diverts trains.

clue.text: A letter from Elizabeth Garret Anderson

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words in the woman's name

explanation.surface: Correspondence arrives from a pioneering Victorian woman doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Garrett Anderson was Britain's first woman doctor; the letter meant is a Greek one, found across 'GarrET Anderson'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh character of the Greek alphabet is a letter.

clue.text: Scramble aboard the bus when Chernobyl is in operation

definitions.meaning: to crowd onto something all at once
a nuclear reactor is called a pile, and when it runs the pile is switched on

explanation.surface: Passengers rush onto a bus while the nuclear plant runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd aggressively onto something is to scramble aboard; a reactor, called a pile, is running when switched on.

clue.text: Tears around river to reveal hidden wealth

indicators.note: the letters of tears are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone weeps by a river, which leads them to buried riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' is the fodder; 'around' rearranges it to TREAS, followed by the river URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarded or buried riches, such as gold or jewels, are a store of concealed valuables.

clue.text: Trouble from the year dot

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks a year of the Christian era
a dot is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Problems have existed from the very beginning of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the year dot' is the idiom for 'since the very beginning'; split up, it gives AD and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and bother is trouble, as in 'much fuss about nothing'.

clue.text: Changed sides when thwarted

definitions.meaning: ... over, as across a road or to the other camp
... in the sense of opposed or frustrated

explanation.surface: Someone switched allegiance after being blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Going over to the other side, and having one's plans opposed or frustrated, share one past-tense verb.

clue.text: Main letters used in 20

indicators.note: says that the answer is a run of letters within another light's solution

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 across

explanation.surface: The chief letters appear in another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is an old word for the ocean; the run is found inside the answer to 20 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean is called the main in poetry, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: One who espies the originator of Gamesmanship

definitions.meaning: someone who watches for and notices things

explanation.surface: A lookout catches the man who first described winning by sly tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter's 1947 book 'Gamesmanship' coined the word; his initial and surname run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher who picks things out, like a plane-watcher; and S. Potter, author of the book.

clue.text: Lads after a job in the mail service

definitions.note: the plural answer names young men working in the postal service

indicators.note: says the boys come after the job in the answer

parts.note: a post is a job or position
lads are boys

explanation.surface: Young men are looking for employment with the post office.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the boys by where they work: lads employed carrying the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys who carried letters or rode post-horses were employed by the postal service.

clue.text: Children needing three lots of singlets?

parts.note: three times over is triple
a singlet is a vest or tee shirt, so several of them are tees, written Ts

explanation.surface: A family needs three times as many vests for their kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'singlets' becomes Ts, tees, multiplied by TRIPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Three offspring born at one birth are a set of siblings, all children.

clue.text: Speech describing Christian habit

parts.note: AD, anno domini, names the Christian era
a habit is a form of dress, as worn by a monk or nun

explanation.surface: A talk describes what a Christian religious wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a nun's robe, and does mean dress here.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk to an audience is a speech.

clue.text: Died swallowing lots of water when infected

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: taken as written
seas are great bodies of water

explanation.surface: Someone perished after drinking too much water while ill.
explanation.walkthrough: DIED swallows SEAS: DI-SEAS-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infected is sick or affected by illness.

clue.text: I enter amended total

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keys in a corrected sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and complete, as in a total or unbroken amount.

clue.text: Nuts to gather not far from Croydon

indicators.note: to gather the letters is to pull them together into a new order

explanation.surface: Nut gatherers head to a spot near a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Croydon and Sutton are neighbouring boroughs of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbouring borough of south London lies close by Croydon.

clue.text: Solar winds taking in one accustomed to terrestrial ones

indicators.note: winds as a verb, twisting the letters into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Winds from the sun contrast with someone used to winds on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' turns SOLAR to SALOR, which takes in I. The definition sets the seafarer's earthly winds against the 'solar winds' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer lives by the winds that blow on earth, being used to them at sea.

clue.text: Spot nothing in the initial version of this paper

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.words: the initial version of this paper
parts.note: DT, the initials of the Daily Telegraph, the paper carrying the puzzle
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing appears in an early edition of the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial version' reads as first edition; it means the paper's initials, D and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round mark is a spot.

clue.text: Will writer try out the first 18 letters?

parts.note: to try something out is to test it
the alphabet from A to R covers eighteen letters

explanation.surface: An author wonders whether to try out part of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is a testament, not a name; the 18 letters run A to R, written as A TO R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has made a legal testament is its author.

clue.text: Sick in the forepart of the ship? Must be the ocean wave

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Seasickness strikes at the front of a ship in heavy waves.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL goes inside BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A great rolling swell of the sea is a large wave.

clue.text: Timid method, but it has a sensational response

parts.note: timid means nervous
a system is a method

explanation.surface: A shy procedure still provokes a dramatic reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensational' means relating to the senses, not dramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's network of nerves carries sensation and responds to stimuli.
